LOCATION PLATE — CHEN'S ROOM, DAY (EMPTY)
No reference images. Build the location entirely from the description below.

WHAT THIS IMAGE IS
A single wide photograph of one room, shot empty and tidy, to be used as a reusable location reference. NO PEOPLE ARE IN THE FRAME. Horizontal 16:9 frame.

THE CAMERA POSITION — STANDING AT THE WINDOW, LOOKING INTO THE ROOM
THE CAMERA STANDS WITH ITS BACK TO THE WINDOW and LOOKS INTO THE ROOM toward the far corner where the bed wall meets the dressing-room wall.
THE WINDOW IS BEHIND THE CAMERA AND IS NOT IN THE PICTURE AT ALL. No window, no glass, no frame, no sill, no bright white panel and no view appears anywhere in the frame. The daylight arrives from directly behind the lens and falls forward into the room.

THE ROOM
A large, high-ceilinged room in the modern wing of a family house, about three and a half metres to the ceiling. Calm, expensive and in good order.
THE PALETTE: a deep warm OLIVE-GREEN plaster wall behind the bed, CHALK-WHITE plaster elsewhere, DARK WALNUT herringbone floor, CARAMEL-TAN LEATHER, OATMEAL and CREAM textiles, one note of TERRACOTTA, with raw grey CONCRETE and BLACKENED STEEL as the structure.

THE LAYOUT AS SEEN FROM THE CAMERA
ON THE LEFT OF FRAME, THE LONG BED WALL runs away from the camera: DEEP WARM OLIVE-GREEN hand-trowelled plaster with faint cloudy tonal variation and a soft matte finish. A BROAD RAW CONCRETE BEAM runs across the top of it, rough and board-marked, with chalk-white plaster above to the ceiling.
AGAINST THAT WALL, in the middle distance, THE BED, seen from its side and slightly from the foot: a low, very wide platform bed, NEATLY MADE in crisp cream linen, the duvet smooth and squared off, an oatmeal wool throw folded in a clean band across the foot, and four pillows stacked tidily — two cream, one stone, one terracotta. A LONG CARAMEL-TAN TUFTED LEATHER BENCH sits across the foot of the bed on slim black legs, bare and clear.
BEYOND THE BED, A LOW WALNUT SIDEBOARD on slim legs, with a small unlit ceramic lamp at one end and a neat stack of books squared up at the other.
A TALL SLIM BLACK FLOOR LAMP with a flat white dome shade stands at the head of the bed, UNLIT.
ABOVE THE SIDEBOARD, A SHORT BLACK FLOATING SHELF holds three pairs of sneakers set out evenly — one cream, one olive, one terracotta.
STRAIGHT AHEAD, FILLING THE FAR CORNER, BLACK STEEL-FRAMED SLIDING DOORS WITH REEDED GLASS, tall panels divided by fine black crossbars, the ribbed glass blurring the hanging clothes behind them. All panels are closed.
ON THE RIGHT, the chalk-white right-hand wall comes toward the camera. Against it A TALL FULL-HEIGHT MIRROR IN A SLIM BLACKENED STEEL FRAME STANDS UPRIGHT, LEANING BACK, about two metres tall, reflecting the olive wall and the walnut floor. Beside it, nearer the camera, A SLIM BLACK TUBULAR STAND carries A MATTE BLACK MOTORCYCLE HELMET at shoulder height with a pair of black riding boots set neatly on its lower rail.
IN THE NEAR FOREGROUND, entering from the bottom left and seen from behind, A LOW SOFA in OATMEAL BOUCLÉ facing into the room, cushions sitting square, with a small round walnut side table beside it carrying one closed book.
NEAR THE CAMERA END OF THE OLIVE WALL, A BLACK ACOUSTIC GUITAR stands upright on a slim stand, with a small neat stack of vinyl records squared against the wall beside it.
THE FLOOR is DARK WALNUT in a wide herringbone running away from the camera, clean and clear. A large OATMEAL flat-weave rug lies squarely between the sofa and the bed, straight and flat.
THE CEILING is chalk white and flat.
THE ROOM IS TIDY AND PUT AWAY — the floor is clear, every surface is uncluttered, nothing is dropped, draped, crumpled or left lying about.

LIGHTING
THE ROOM IS LIT ENTIRELY BY DAYLIGHT COMING FROM BEHIND THE CAMERA, through the window that is out of shot. Broad, soft and even, washing forward and lighting the whole room almost uniformly.
THE PICTURE IS BRIGHT AND WELL EXPOSED, open and fully legible, with gentle soft shadows falling away from the camera and only a mild falloff into the far corner. Nothing murky, nothing crushed.
THE WHITE BALANCE IS TRUE AND NEUTRAL — the plaster reads clean white, the olive reads olive, the walnut reads brown, the caramel reads tan.
EVERY LAMP IS SWITCHED OFF — dark objects only, no glow anywhere.
No sun patches, no shafts, no flare.

OPTICS
35mm-equivalent look, about a 63° diagonal field of view. Camera at 1.4 metres, level, far corner slightly left of centre. Moderate aperture, the whole room in focus from the foreground sofa to the far corner.

STYLE — PLAIN AND NEUTRAL
AN ORDINARY, HONEST PHOTOGRAPH OF A REAL ROOM — the kind of plain establishing frame a Korean drama uses to show where someone lives. The treatment is completely neutral and gets out of the way: the room itself does all the work.
Flat, even, natural light with no shaping and no mood. True-to-life colour, straight out of camera, with a neutral grade — NO teal-and-orange, NO warm filter, NO cool filter, NO heavy contrast, NO crushed blacks, NO lifted film blacks.
A CLEAN DIGITAL CAPTURE: smooth and natural, with NO film grain, NO halation, NO glow, NO bloom, NO vignette, NO lens flare and NO artistic texture laid over the picture.
Framing is simple and unfussy, straight on, composed by eye rather than perfectly symmetrical. Everyday realism in the materials — real fabric, real wood, real plaster — with no stylisation in the photography.

QUALITY
Natural clarity with real material texture — the trowel marks in the olive plaster, the board-marked concrete, the grain of the walnut herringbone, the soft sheen and deep buttoning of the caramel leather, the loop of the bouclé, the weave of the linen, the ribs of the reeded glass. Stable geometry, upright verticals, no barrel distortion, no fisheye bulge. Believable scale and proportion against the three-and-a-half-metre ceiling.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
THE ROOM IS TIDY AND IN ORDER — the bed is neatly made, the floor is clear, every surface is uncluttered. There are no clothes, shoes, towels, cables, glasses, papers or objects left lying about anywhere.
THE PHOTOGRAPH ITSELF IS PLAIN AND NEUTRAL — natural colour, flat even light, clean capture, no grain, no vignette, no glow, no colour grade, no stylisation of any kind.
THERE IS NO WINDOW ANYWHERE IN THE FRAME — no glass, no window frame, no sill, no bright white panel, no view. The light comes from behind the camera.
THE PICTURE IS BRIGHT AND EVENLY EXPOSED, every part of the frame clearly visible.
EVERY LAMP IS SWITCHED OFF AND DARK.
THE OLIVE PLASTER WALL WITH THE CONCRETE BEAM RUNS DOWN THE LEFT SIDE, with the neatly made bed against it seen from the side.
THE BLACK STEEL REEDED-GLASS DRESSING-ROOM DOORS FILL THE FAR CORNER AHEAD, closed.
THE TALL FULL-HEIGHT MIRROR STANDS UPRIGHT AGAINST THE RIGHT-HAND WALL, with the black helmet stand beside it nearer the camera.
A LOW OATMEAL SOFA SITS IN THE NEAR FOREGROUND, seen from behind.
THE ROOM IS COMPLETELY EMPTY OF PEOPLE — no person, no figure, no silhouette, no reflection of a person in the mirror or the glass.
IT IS ONE SINGLE WIDE PHOTOGRAPH OF ONE ROOM, not a panel sheet and not a collage.
ALL VERTICAL LINES STAY VERTICAL and the camera is level.
There is no text, no writing, no signage, no posters, no logos, no brand marks and no lettering anywhere in the frame, including on the sneakers, the helmet, the books and the records.

LOCATION PLATE — JENNY'S DRESSING ROOM, DAY (EMPTY, PARTIAL VIEW)
No reference images. Build the location entirely from the description below.

WHAT THIS IMAGE IS
A single photograph of PART OF a large private dressing room, shot empty and tidy, to be used as a reusable location reference. NO PEOPLE ARE IN THE FRAME. Horizontal 16:9 frame.

THIS IS A CROP OF THE ROOM, NOT THE WHOLE ROOM
The camera is up on the balcony gallery, looking DOWN AND ACROSS the open void to the opposite side. We see ONE SLICE of a much bigger space, and it is obvious the room carries on past every edge:
— THE CHANDELIER IS CUT OFF BY THE TOP EDGE, so only its long tapering lower cascade hangs down through the middle of the frame; its top, its fixing and the ceiling are all out of shot.
— THE BALCONY AND ITS RAILING RUN OUT OF FRAME AT BOTH THE LEFT AND RIGHT EDGES.
— THE CARPET AND THE FLOOR CASE BELOW ARE CUT OFF BY THE BOTTOM EDGE.
— THE CEILING, THE DOME AND THE STAIRCASE ARE NOT IN SHOT AT ALL.
It reads as a casual frame taken while leaning on the gallery rail, not as a composed architectural portrait of the whole room.

THE ROOM — A HUGE PRIVATE DRESSING ROOM, TWO STOREYS HIGH
A grand circular dressing room in a very wealthy private house, open through two floors with a balcony gallery running round at the upper level. Built entirely for clothes: every curved wall surface is rails, shelves and niches. Immaculate, serene and absurdly luxurious.
THE PALETTE: cream and ivory millwork, soft blush wool carpet, pale stone, antique silver and clear crystal, with the only strong colour coming from the clothes — rows of soft pastels, pale pinks, mints, lilacs, creams and a few deeper tones.

WHAT IS IN THE FRAME

ACROSS THE UPPER THIRD, THE BALCONY GALLERY ON THE FAR SIDE: its edge formed by AN ORNATE WHITE WROUGHT-IRON RAILING of fine scrolled S-curves and leaf shapes, delicate and airy, running horizontally across the picture and cut off at both side edges.
BEHIND THAT RAILING, on the upper level: long OPEN HANGING BAYS between slim cream-painted pilasters with soft moulded arches, holding rails of garments on matching pale padded hangers, HUNG IN TIDY COLOUR ORDER — ivory into blush into dusty pink into mint and pale blue, evenly spaced and hanging straight. On the right of the upper level, OPEN NICHES WITH A SOFT CONCEALED LIGHT hold HANDBAGS STANDING IN NEAT ROWS and round hatboxes stacked on the shelf above.
AT THE CENTRE OF THE UPPER WALL, A PAIR OF TALL MIRRORED DOORS in a cream frame with an arched head, reflecting a soft blurred piece of the room back at itself.

THROUGH THE VOID AND DOWN ON THE LOWER LEVEL, seen at a downward angle:
AT THE FAR CURVE, A KIDNEY-SHAPED VANITY TABLE in cream lacquer on slender carved legs, with A TRIPLE ARCHED MIRROR standing on it in a cream frame, its two side panels angled inward, and a small round upholstered chair in pale blush pushed in. On the top, a few plain glass bottles and a lidded trinket box, set out sparsely.
EITHER SIDE OF THE VANITY, more open hanging bays of pastel garments in colour order.
ON THE RIGHT OF THE LOWER LEVEL, A TALL BANK OF OPEN SHOE SHELVES — six narrow shelves holding neat rows of shoes placed in pairs, cream, nude, pale grey and black.
ON THE LEFT OF THE LOWER LEVEL, lower open shelves of shoes and a slim mirrored trolley with two glass tiers carrying folded scarves in pale green and cream.
TWO SMALL ROUND UPHOLSTERED STOOLS in pale blush on slim antique-silver legs stand out on the open floor.

DOWN THE CENTRE OF THE FRAME, THE LOWER CASCADE OF A VAST CRYSTAL CHANDELIER falls through the void — thousands of fine clear crystal strands tapering to a long slender point, passing in front of the balcony railing and reaching down toward the floor below. Its upper tiers are cut off above the top edge of the picture.

AT THE BOTTOM OF THE FRAME, THE LOWER FLOOR: SOFT BLUSH-BEIGE WOOL CARPET, pale and dense, with A LOW OCTAGONAL GLASS-TOPPED DISPLAY CASE set flush into it — a cream frame divided into wedge-shaped compartments, each lined in soft rose fabric and holding plain fine jewellery laid out in rows. The case is partly cut off by the bottom edge of the picture.

THE ROOM IS IMMACULATE — everything hung straight, spaced evenly and put away. Nothing is dropped, draped, crumpled or left lying on the floor.

LIGHTING
SOFT, EVEN, NEUTRAL DAYLIGHT filling the whole volume from above and from off-frame, bouncing off the cream millwork and the pale carpet so EVERY PART OF THE FRAME IS BRIGHT AND CLEARLY READABLE — the upper rails, the railing, the chandelier, the vanity, the shoe shelves and the carpet below.
THE CHANDELIER IS LIT AT A LOW LEVEL WITH A CLEAN NEUTRAL-WHITE LIGHT so the crystal sparkles without tinting the room. The bag niches carry the same soft neutral-white strip light.
THE WHITE BALANCE IS TRUE AND NEUTRAL — cream reads cream, the carpet reads a soft neutral pink, the crystal reads clear. NO warm cast, NO golden tint, NO amber glow, NO blue tint.
THE PICTURE IS BRIGHT AND EVENLY EXPOSED, with gentle open shadows under the gallery and nothing murky or crushed. No sun patches, no shafts, no flare, no starburst on the crystal.

OPTICS
35mm-equivalent look, about a 63° diagonal field of view. Camera at the balcony rail, about 3.5 metres above the lower floor, ANGLED DOWNWARD maybe twenty degrees so we look across and down into the void. Moderate aperture, everything in the frame sharp.

STYLE — PLAIN AND NEUTRAL
AN ORDINARY, HONEST PHOTOGRAPH — the kind of plain frame a Korean drama uses to show a place. The treatment is completely neutral and gets out of the way.
Even natural light with no shaping and no mood. True-to-life colour, straight out of camera, with a neutral grade — NO teal-and-orange, NO pink filter, NO warm filter, NO heavy contrast, NO crushed blacks, NO lifted blacks.
A CLEAN DIGITAL CAPTURE: smooth and natural, with NO film grain, NO halation, NO glow, NO bloom, NO vignette, NO lens flare and NO artistic texture laid over the picture.
Framing is casual and off-centre rather than neatly symmetrical, with elements running off the edges.

QUALITY
Natural clarity with real material texture — the brushed cream paint and crisp mouldings of the millwork, the dense wool pile of the carpet, the fabric and weave of the hanging clothes, the forged curves of the iron railing, the faceted refractions in the crystal, the polish of the glass case. Stable geometry, upright verticals on the pilasters and the mirrored doors, no barrel distortion, no fisheye bulge. Believable scale.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
THE FRAME IS A PARTIAL VIEW — the chandelier is cut off by the top edge, the balcony and railing run off both side edges, the floor and the jewellery case are cut off by the bottom edge, and the room clearly continues beyond the picture on every side.
THE CEILING, THE DOME AND THE STAIRCASE ARE NOT VISIBLE.
THE CAMERA IS UP AT THE BALCONY AND LOOKS DOWN AND ACROSS THE OPEN VOID.
THIS IS A DRESSING ROOM, NOT A BEDROOM — no bed, no headboard, no bedding anywhere.
AN ORNATE WHITE SCROLLED IRON RAILING RUNS ACROSS THE UPPER PART OF THE FRAME with rails of pastel clothes and niches of handbags behind it.
THE LOWER CASCADE OF A CRYSTAL CHANDELIER FALLS DOWN THE CENTRE of the picture.
A CREAM KIDNEY-SHAPED VANITY WITH A TRIPLE ARCHED MIRROR stands on the lower level at the far curve.
A TALL BANK OF OPEN SHOE SHELVES stands on the right of the lower level.
A LOW OCTAGONAL GLASS-TOPPED JEWELLERY CASE IS SET INTO THE BLUSH CARPET at the bottom of the frame, partly cropped.
THE ROOM IS IMMACULATE AND TIDY — nothing dropped, draped or left lying about.
THE PHOTOGRAPH ITSELF IS PLAIN AND NEUTRAL — natural colour, even light, clean capture, no grain, no vignette, no glow, no colour grade.
THE PICTURE IS BRIGHT AND EVENLY EXPOSED across the whole frame.
THE ROOM IS COMPLETELY EMPTY OF PEOPLE — no person, no figure, no silhouette, no reflection of a person in any mirror.
IT IS ONE SINGLE PHOTOGRAPH, not a panel sheet and not a collage.
EVERY BAG, SHOE, BOX, BOTTLE AND PIECE OF JEWELLERY IS A PLAIN, GENERIC, ORIGINAL OBJECT — simple shapes and plain colours, with no recognisable design, no monogram, no hardware motif and no branding.
There is no text, no writing, no signage, no logos, no brand marks and no lettering anywhere in the frame.
